correctness.rationale: For each prime divisor q of b-1, avoiding 1+c+jd=0 for 0<=j<=p-2 is possible because either q divides d (one excluded class) or q>=p (at most p-1 excluded classes); CRT gives c. The bound (p-2)d<=b+1 makes c+jd<2b, so the only possible carry is e_j in {0,1}. For S_j=1+s_b(c+jd), gcd(S_j,b-1)=1. Simultaneously take b^m congruent to b modulo every prime dividing the finite product of S_j, possible by Fermat and direct divisibility; n_j=b^m+c+jd then has digit sum S_j. A common prime divisor would divide (b-1)(1+e_j), whose prime support is contained in b-1 since b is odd, contradiction. The matching p-term obstruction follows from p|b-1, p not dividing d, and s_b(n)=n mod p. The fully quantified proof is independent of the recorded 1343-parameter finite checker.

originality.rationale: Blau et al. provide the p-1 upper bound and the d=2 case and state the even-difference attainment as Conjecture 4.3. The present proof covers a specified short-even-stride region, especially every odd base with 5|(b-1), 3 not dividing (b-1) at d=4. Checked accessible sources and mathematical records did not identify the same statement or a stronger implication. One related alternative construction imposes an additional auxiliary prime-coprimality restriction and a larger base threshold; this theorem includes cases outside it. Unindexed later work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A differently indexed proof of Conjecture 4.3 or of the same short-stride parameter region may exist outside the inspected sources.

value.rationale: Settles a natural nontrivial parameter region of an expressly published anti-Niven arithmetic-progression conjecture, including the first unsolved-looking even stride d=4 in an entire infinite family of bases. It gives infinitely many extremal starts with no auxiliary factor-coprimality restriction, not mere numerical exceptions. The two-digit carry bound explains the mathematical parameter boundary and suggests what new ideas would be needed beyond it.
